note: COUNTING CONVENTION: the paper's '7 unary, 9 binary, 12 rolling operators over 9 signals' counts DISTINCT operator NAMES PER KIND, matching operator_counts_by_kind above; do NOT sum across kinds (7+9+12=28 is not a meaningful figure). Some operator names (Max, Min, Rank) intentionally appear under more than one kind because they denote different operations there (e.g. binary Max(a,b) vs rolling Max over a window); the node's kind field selects the handler in evaluate_factors.py. The unary/binary/rolling lists reflect that evaluator's per-kind dispatch exactly.
